questionText: Which one of the following statements is TRUE ?

options.html: Cant deficiency is related to train moving faster, and Cant excess is related to train moving slower.
options.text: Cant deficiency is related to train moving faster, and Cant excess is related to train moving slower.

options.html: Cant deficiency is related to train moving slower, and Cant excess is related to train moving faster.
options.text: Cant deficiency is related to train moving slower, and Cant excess is related to train moving faster.

options.html: Cant deficiency is related to train moving on the main line, and Cant excess is related to train moving on the branch line.
options.text: Cant deficiency is related to train moving on the main line, and Cant excess is related to train moving on the branch line.

options.html: Cant deficiency is related to train moving on the branch line, and Cant excess is related to train moving on the main line.
options.text: Cant deficiency is related to train moving on the branch line, and Cant excess is related to train moving on the main line.

explanationHtml:
Definitions:

Cant (superelevation): The outer rail is raised above the inner rail to counteract centrifugal force at a given equilibrium speed.

Cant deficiency: Occurs when a train moves faster than the equilibrium speed for which the cant is designed. The centrifugal force exceeds the component provided by the cant - the effective cant is less than needed. Train tends to overturn outward.

Cant excess: Occurs when a train moves slower than the equilibrium speed. The cant provides more than needed - the train tends to slip inward toward the inner rail.

Therefore, Option (A) is correct.

explanationHtml:
Let's examine each option to find the FALSE statement.
Option A: The compressive strength of a concrete specimen can vary depending on its shape and size.
This is true. The shape (cube vs. cylinder) and size of a specimen affect the test results due to variations in stress distribution and failure patterns.

Option B: Air-dried and saturated test specimens show the same compressive strength for concrete.
This is false. Air-dried specimens typically show higher compressive strength compared to saturated ones because excess moisture can weaken the internal structure during loading.

Option C: Curing conditions, such as temperature and relative humidity, can influence the compressive strength of concrete.
This is true. Proper curing ensures complete hydration and strength development, while poor curing can reduce final strength.

Option D: Compressive strength depends on the water-to-binder ratio used in the concrete mixture.
This is true. Lower water-to-binder ratios generally result in higher strength due to denser microstructure and improved bonding.

Annual depreciation (D),

SOY Method (Sum of year Digit)
SOY=n(n+1)2=5×62=15dm=n−(m−1)SOYDm=(P−SV)×dmBVm=BVm−1−Dmd1=5−(1−1)15=515D1=(1,60,000−10,000)×515=50,000d2=415;    D2=40,000d3=315;    D3=30,000d4=215;    D4=20,000d5=215;    D2=10,000BV0=1,60,000BV1=1,60,000−50,000=1,10,000BV2=1,10,000−40,000=70,000BV3=70,000−30,000=40,000BV4=40,000−20,000=20,000BV5=20,000−10,000=10,000\begin{aligned} SOY&=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}=\frac{5 \times 6}{2}=15 \\ d_m&=\frac{n-(m-1)}{SOY} \\ D_m&=(P-SV) \times d_m \\ BV_m&=BV_{m-1}-D_m \\ d_1&= \frac{5-(1-1)}{15}=\frac{5}{15}\\ D_1&= (1,60,000-10,000) \times \frac{5}{15} \\ &=50,000\\ d_2&=\frac{4}{15} ; \;\;D_2=40,000\\ d_3&=\frac{3}{15} ; \;\;D_3=30,000\\ d_4&=\frac{2}{15} ; \;\;D_4=20,000\\ d_5&=\frac{2}{15} ; \;\;D_2=10,000\\ BV_0&=1,60,000 \\ BV_1&=1,60,000 -50,000=1,10,000 \\ BV_2&=1,10,000 -40,000=70,000 \\ BV_3&=70,000 -30,000=40,000 \\ BV_4&=40,000 -20,000=20,000 \\ BV_5&=20,000 -10,000=10,000 \\ \end{aligned}SOYdm​Dm​BVm​d1​D1​d2​d3​d4​d5​BV0​BV1​BV2​BV3​BV4​BV5​​=2n(n+1)​=25×6​=15=SOYn−(m−1)​=(P−SV)×dm​=BVm−1​−Dm​=155−(1−1)​=155​=(1,60,000−10,000)×155​=50,000=154​;D2​=40,000=153​;D3​=30,000=152​;D4​=20,000=152​;D2​=10,000=1,60,000=1,60,000−50,000=1,10,000=1,10,000−40,000=70,000=70,000−30,000=40,000=40,000−20,000=20,000=20,000−10,000=10,000​

questionText: For a construction project, the mean and standard deviation of the completion time are 200 days and 6.1 days, respectively. Assume normal distribution and use the value of standard normal deviate Z = 1.64 for the 95% confidence level. The maximum time required (in days) for the completion of the project would be _______
explanationText: Expected completion time of project, $\; T_{E\, project}=200\, days$ Standard deviation of project, $\begin{aligned} \sigma _{project}&=6.1\, days\\ Z&= \frac{T_{S}-T_{E}}{\sigma _{project}} \\ &=\frac{T_{S}-T_{E\, project}}{\sigma _{project}}\\ 1.64&= \frac{T_{S}-200}{6.1}\\ T_{S}&=200+6.1\times 1.64\\ &=200+10.004\\ &=210.004 \simeq 210\, days \end{aligned}$
